title: Is an Electron a Cloud? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A ceiling fan spins so fast that its blades become a blur, and a weather report only gives a chance of rain. An electron in an atom is like that blur, only stranger: we can only give chances. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we follow Aarav's question into the quantum mechanical model of the atom.

We see why Bohr's neat circles had to go (electrons are waves, and their exact path can never be known), meet Schrodinger's equation (1926) in its short form, H psi = E psi, and then build an orbital on the molecule bench: the wave function psi, the probability density psi squared, and thousands of dots that gather into a probability cloud around a hydrogen nucleus. An orbit and an orbital go side by side, the features of the model follow link by link (quantised energy, orbitals as wave functions, psi squared as probability, at most two electrons per orbital), and a worked example shows why a negative psi can still mean the most likely place. Then what the model fixed, the exam trap on psi vs psi squared, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 21 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
